title: Magnetic properties and Fermi-surface topology of kagome magnet HoV$_6$Sn$_6$
authors: Tucker Beekmann, Ganesh Pokharel, Wyatt Edward Ackerman, Stephen D. Wilson, David E. Graf, Keshav Shrestha
abstract: We report a study of the magnetic properties and Fermi-surface topology of the kagome magnet HoV$_6$Sn$_6$ using magnetization and tunnel-diode-oscillator (TDO) measurements. The temperature-dependent magnetization exhibits Curie-Weiss behavior at high temperatures and reveals long-range magnetic order below $T_c$ $\approx$ 2.4 K. Below Tc, the field-dependent magnetization reveals pronounced magnetic anisotropy, with saturation moments of $\approx$ 9.5 and 7 $μ_B$ /Ho for fields applied along the out-of-plane and in-plane directions, respectively. To probe the Fermi surface, we perform TDO measurements in magnetic fields up to 41.5 T and at temperatures down to 0.35 K. The TDO signal exhibits well-defined quantum oscillations with multiple frequencies extending up to $\sim$ 9 kT. Angular- and temperature-dependent measurements are used to determine the Fermi-surface geometry and cyclotron effective masses, respectively. To elucidate the electronic structure, we perform first-principles calculations of the electronic bands, density of states (DOS), and Fermi surface. The calculated band structure exhibits flat-band features, van Hove singularities, and Dirac-like crossings near the Fermi level. The DOS near the Fermi level is dominated by the V-d orbitals, indicating that the V kagome layers play a major role in determining the low-energy electronic properties of HoV6Sn6. Our calculations further support a ferromagnetic ground state with the Ho moments oriented along the c axis, consistent with neutron-scattering measurements. The calculated quantum-oscillation frequencies from the Fermi-surface pockets of HoV6Sn6 are in overall good agreement with the experimentally observed frequencies. Our combined experimental and theoretical results provide insight into the magnetic anisotropy and electronic structure of HoV$_6$Sn$_6$ and reveal its multiband Fermi-surface topology.
summary: This work comprehensively characterizes the magnetic and electronic properties of the kagome magnet HoV6Sn6. By combining magnetization measurements, quantum oscillation experiments, and DFT calculations, the authors establish strong magnetic anisotropy and map out a complex, multiband Fermi surface. The results highlight the crucial role of the V-d orbitals in determining the low-energy electronic behavior of this material.
main_problem: The study investigates the magnetic properties and Fermi-surface topology of the kagome magnet HoV6Sn6.
main_result: The research reveals strong magnetic anisotropy favoring c-axis alignment and identifies a multiband Fermi-surface topology, with electronic properties dominated by V-d orbitals.
method: The study combines magnetization measurements, low-temperature quantum oscillation measurements (TDO), and first-principles electronic structure calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is HoV6Sn6, a kagome lattice magnet. The electronic structure is modeled using DFT calculations, revealing features like flat bands and van Hove singularities near the Fermi level.
key_observables: Temperature-dependent magnetization, magnetic anisotropy (saturation moments), quantum oscillation frequencies, and Fermi-surface geometry.
important_parameters: Critical temperature $T_c \approx 2.4 \text{ K}$; magnetic fields up to 41.5 T; effective mass $m^* = 0.64(6)m_e$.
main_assumptions: The high-temperature susceptibility follows Curie-Weiss behavior, and the temperature dependence of quantum oscillations is analyzed using the Lifshitz–Kosevich formalism.
figures_summary: Figures show magnetic susceptibility vs. temperature, field-dependent magnetization revealing anisotropy, and TDO spectra displaying multiple quantum oscillation frequencies whose angular dependence maps Fermi-surface pockets.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by characterizing the magnetic ordering via magnetization measurements, then probes the electronic structure and Fermi surface using TDO quantum oscillations, and finally corroborates these findings with first-principles calculations of the band structure and DOS.
why_interesting: The interplay between magnetic ordering, complex Fermi surface topology, and strong electronic correlations (V-d orbital dominance) in a geometrically frustrated kagome lattice is highly relevant to understanding strongly correlated electron systems.
